caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: SPARC:108
attempts.entry_title: Imaging acetylcholine release with a DNA nanosensor (Xia et al. 2021)
attempts.summary: Of the paper's main in vivo findings, the vesamicol block of the nanosensor signal and its rostral to caudal spread across the ganglion held up in part, each in the one experiment or mouse deposited; the spread's timings did not match. The ex vivo Michaelis-Menten calibration and the size of the evoked response did not reproduce: the deposited recordings rise by 17.1 to 40.1% where the paper reports 3.7%, and no file records when stimulation began or ACh was added. The control nanosensor tests ruling out pH effects, and the voltage and pulse dose responses, are untestable, as those recordings are not deposited. The sensor's gel bands and receptor staining reproduced, and its placement on somata in part.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Xia, Yang, Mu, Micovic, Poskanzer, Monaghan and Clark (2021) on SPARC:108, which holds the nanosensor's HPLC, UV-Vis and gel data, ex vivo calibration recordings of one mouse, in vivo recordings at 3, 8 and 10 V, a confocal stack of a stained ganglion and one vesamicol experiment, and on SPARC:75, which holds confocal images of a ganglion stained with BTX or the nanosensor. The control nanosensor, pH, voltage and pulse series, AFM, stability and two-photon data are not deposited, and the AQuA analysis was not run.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Xia et al. (2021) from SPARC:108 and SPARC:75

outcomes.statement: In size-exclusion HPLC the assembled nanosensors elute first (main peak near 7.5 mL), followed by a second peak at 9.1 to 9.2 mL of unreacted material, and the nanosensors are about 77% of the reaction mixture by area under all peaks of the pHAb channel.
outcomes.source: Results, Fabrication and in vitro characterization, paragraph 2 (beginning "Fully assembled ACh nanosensors were purified"); Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: ACh nanosensors represent ∼77% of the reaction mixture based on the integration of areas under all detectable peaks from the pHAb channel chromatogram
outcomes.notes: The pHAb chromatogram (HPLC_PHAB.csv) has two detectable peaks, at 15.16 and 18.05 min. The share of the first peak depends on the reading. With a flat baseline (reading a) it is 65.8 to 68.2% under every end of the second peak, below the tolerance of 69.3 to 84.7%, and with a common line under both peaks and a drop at the valley 66.2 to 69.1%. With a line under each peak (reading b, as the criterion writes it) it is 77.5 to 83.1%, within tolerance, when the second peak ends where its own descent ends (20.53 min) or where it falls below 2% of its height (20.94 min); when it ends where the signal returns to the pre-injection level (29.76 min) the second area is negative and no share can be read. 4 of 18 readings are within tolerance. The valley between the peaks is 5.19 high (main peak 13.62), so the line under each peak cuts through both peaks; it keeps 54% of the main peak's area above the flat baseline and 30% (end ii) or 23% (end iii) of the second peak's. Every reading that splits the overlap the usual way (flat baseline, or a common line with a drop at the valley) gives 65.8 to 69.1%, just below tolerance, so the share holds by the letter of reading (b) only. The retention volumes are not tested, as the paper gives no flow rate; the ratio of the retention times, 1.191, is 1.8% below the paper's 1.213 to 1.227. Partially reproduced, as the share holds under one reading of the criterion and the volume part cannot be tested. Measured is the share under reading (b), the second peak ending at the end of its descent, 1% detection rule.
deviations: The paper gives no flow rate (Methods name the Superdex 200 increase 10/300 GL column and the Agilent Infinity 1260 HPLC only), and the files give time, so the main and second peak volumes are not tested. The first version assumed 0.5 mL/min, chosen because it put the peaks at the paper's volumes, which made that test circular.
"Detectable" peaks taken as those with a prominence of at least 1% of the largest (0.5% as a variant), a choice made here.

Assumed that the second peak ends where its own descent ends (slope below 1% of the steepest, 20.53 min), the usual limit of a peak; ends where it falls below 2% of its height and where the signal returns to the pre-injection level + 3 SD (29.76 min, the first version) are shown. The share under reading (b) depends on it.

outcomes.statement: By Beer-Lambert estimates at 260, 280 and 652 nm, the nanosensor carries 2.86 AChE, 1.70 BTX and 3.85 pHAb per DNA scaffold, conjugation efficiencies of 71%, 85% and 96%.
outcomes.source: Results, Fabrication and in vitro characterization, the text around and after Equations 1 and 2; Figure 2F and 2G
outcomes.quote: the conju-gation ratios of AChE, BTX, and pHAb to DNA scaffold were determined to be 2.86, 1.70, and 3.85 (Fig. 2G). The conjugation efficiency of BTX and pHAb reached 85 and 96%, respectively.
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the absorbance spectra of pure DNA scaffold, AChE and BTX to estimate the extinction coefficients of Equations 1 and 2. The deposit holds UV-Vis spectra of the nanosensor (eight repeats, a reblank and water, 2019-08-09_sensor.xml) and of the DNA scaffold (2019-08-09_dna_scaffold.xml) only; there are no spectra of AChE or BTX. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: In native PAGE the purified nanosensor runs as several bands of lower mobility than the DNA scaffold (likely 1 to 4 AChE per scaffold), and these bands carry both pHAb and AF647 fluorescence.
outcomes.source: Results, Fabrication and in vitro characterization, paragraph 2 (beginning "Fully assembled ACh nanosensors were purified"); Figure 2E; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: several bands with lower mo-bility were identified likely due to variable numbers of AChE (from 1 to 4) conjugated to the DNA scaffold (Fig. 2E). Bands that presumptively contain ACh nanosensors displayed overlapping fluorescence of pHAb and AF647
outcomes.notes: Ethidium image, lane 3 (main peak) has two bands (rows 511 and 593) between the well and the scaffold band of lane 1 (row 878). In the registered pHAb and AF647 images lane 3 has pHAb bands at rows 783 and 861, above the pHAb-labelled scaffold band of lane 1 (row 1119), and AF647 bands at rows 783 and 859, 8 and 10 SD above the gel between lanes. Lane 1 of the fluorescence images has a single pHAb band and no AF647 band above background, as for a scaffold without BTX, which fits Figure 2E's label of lane 1 and not Figure S2C's.
deviations: Lanes found as runs of columns with signal and bands as lane-profile peaks with a prominence of at least 5% of the profile range, choices made here as the paper gives no quantification. The ethidium image is framed differently from the fluorescence pair, so band positions are compared within each.

outcomes.statement: The nanosensor is 10 to 20 nm across, by structural simulation and atomic force microscopy, against about 130 nm for the earlier version.
outcomes.source: Results, Fabrication and in vitro characterization, the text after Equations 1 and 2; Figure S3
outcomes.quote: the current ACh nanosensor had an overall size of 10 to 20 nm confirmed by both structural simulations and atomic force microscopy (SI Appendix, Fig. S3)
outcomes.notes: The claim rests on the AFM images of Figure S3B. No AFM file is in either dataset. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: Ex vivo staining of freshly isolated SMG with BTX-AF647 shows a punctate pattern across the ganglion, confirming nicotinic ACh receptors on SMG neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, ACh nanosensors in SMG, paragraph 1; Figure S5
outcomes.quote: Ex vivo staining of freshly isolated SMG with BTX-AF647 showed the expected punctate staining pattern across the ganglion, confirming expres-sion of nicotinic ACh receptors in SMG neurons
outcomes.notes: Judged by eye on the maximum projections and brightest planes of the two BTX stacks of SPARC:75 (GFP and AF647 by the dye names in the LSM metadata). AF647 puncta cover every tile over the GFP mask in all four images (5/5 to 29/29 with the Otsu mask), at 4.4 to 15.8 puncta per 100 um^2 with the background rule used since round 1 (17.8 to 64.4 with the first rule, which passed much of the noise), and lie along the borders of the somata. Nearness to GFP beyond chance holds in three of the four images by at least one mask (low-magnification projection 0.82 of puncta within 1 um of the Otsu GFP mask against 0.37 of the field; its brightest plane 0.61 against 0.24 with the background-rule mask; high-magnification projection 0.18 against 0.15), and not in the brightest high-magnification plane (0.10 against 0.11). The high-magnification stack holds data in 12 of its 62 planes.
deviations: Puncta defined as components above the median + 3 SD of the lower half of the pixels reflected about the median, 0.1 to 25 um^2, and the GFP mask by Otsu's threshold or the same background rule; the first rule (mean + 3 SD of the below-median pixels) is shown as a variant. The paper gives no quantification, and these support, not replace, the judgement by eye the criterion asks for.

outcomes.statement: Confocal imaging of a nanosensor-stained SMG shows punctate AF647 and pHAb staining that overlaps and lies mainly on the neuronal cell soma, consistent with the BTX staining.
outcomes.source: Results, ACh nanosensors in SMG, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Confocal microscopy further confirmed that the punctate staining pattern of AF647 and pHAb were primarily localized on the neuronal cell soma (Fig. 3D).
outcomes.notes: SPARC:108 sub-5 (CZI; AF647, pHAb as AF532, EGFP; 27 planes, 17.41 um, as the Methods state) and the three nanosensor images of SPARC:75. By eye (merges and a full-resolution crop with each channel alone), puncta appear in both channels with yellow spots where they coincide, but much AF647 lines cell borders and the ganglion capsule, and the coinciding spots lie mostly between or at the edges of the somata. With the background rule used since round 1, which marks 7 to 12% of the field as pHAb in four of five images (35% in sub-5 plane 13), 59 to 85% of AF647 puncta overlap pHAb in those four, against 39 to 53% with the pHAb mask shifted by 5 um (top-hat pHAb 68 to 79% against 40 to 64%); in plane 13, 98% against 95%. The first rule marked 32 to 48% of the field and gave 84 to 98% against 78 to 98%. 9 to 47% of AF647 puncta lie in an Otsu soma mask covering 23 to 42% of the field, and 15 to 52% of the coinciding puncta lie within 1 um of it, against 27 to 48% of the field. Reading (b) fails in every image (0.09 to 0.35; 0.13 to 0.40 with a top-hat pHAb and a 1 um margin). In sub-5 the pHAb channel correlates with GFP (r 0.43 and 0.53), a sign of GFP bleed-through at 514 nm. Partially reproduced, as the puncta coincide beyond chance but their place on the somata is not shown.
deviations: Assumed that the by-eye reading (a) is judged together with chance references, a 5 um shift of the pHAb mask and the share of the field covered by the soma mask, as the paper gives no colocalisation measure; the shift, the punctum size limits (0.1 to 25 um^2) and the soma masks (Otsu, background rule, 1 um margin) are choices made here.

The background of the claims file's mean + 3 SD threshold is not defined in the paper. Since round 1 it is the lower half of the pixels reflected about the median (threshold median + 3 SD), the usual half-Gaussian estimate; the first rule, mean + 3 SD of the below-median pixels, sets the threshold about 1 SD above the centre of a Gaussian and marked a third or more of the field, and is shown as a variant.
SPARC:75's nanosensor images are single planes and are used with the sub-5 stack.

outcomes.statement: After rinsing, a substantial amount of nanosensor stays in the SMG, while DNA structures lacking AChE and BTX are barely visible in the tissue.
outcomes.source: Results, ACh nanosensors in SMG, paragraph 2; Figure 3B and 3C
outcomes.quote: In contrast, DNA structures that did not have the AChE and tar-geting ligands (i.e., BTX) were barely visible inside the tissue (Fig. 3C).
outcomes.notes: Needs widefield images of the SMG after washing for the nanosensor (Fig. 3B) and for bare DNA structures (Fig. 3C). Neither dataset has them. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: Nanosensors in the harvested SMG keep their structure and AChE activity for 5 h; after 5 h, adding 100 uM ACh raises the pHAb fluorescence of three ROIs by 20 to 45%.
outcomes.source: Results, ACh nanosensors in SMG, paragraph 2; Figure S4D to F
outcomes.quote: The fluorescence intensity of three ROIs increased by 20-45% after the addition of ACh, indicating that the AChE was still functional and remained conjugated on the DNA scaffold.
outcomes.notes: Needs the confocal images at 0 h and 5 h after harvesting and the ACh test of Figure S4D to F. Not in either dataset. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: The ex vivo nanosensor response to added ACh begins within 0.55 s, the shortest sampling interval used.
outcomes.source: Results, Ex vivo calibration of the ACh nanosensors, paragraph 1; Figure S6A
outcomes.quote: the initial nanosensor response to ACh addition was within 0.55 s, the minimum sampling time used in our experiment
outcomes.notes: The ex vivo calibration recordings (sub-1) are in the dataset, but the time of ACh addition is not recorded, and the files, resaved in ImageJ, keep only the first frame's timestamp. Six of the eight rise by 19.8 to 58.4% within one frame, at frame 7 to 9; as the criterion says, taking the onset from the response would make the test circular.

outcomes.statement: The initial rate of the ex vivo nanosensor response follows a Michaelis-Menten curve in ACh concentration with EC50 (Km) 49.24 ± 5.84 uM and Vmax 281.00 ± 7.14 %/s (R2 0.9811); the upper limit of detection is 358.01 uM.
outcomes.source: Results, Ex vivo calibration of the ACh nanosensors, paragraph 2; Figure 4B legend
outcomes.quote: the half-maximum response (EC50) to ACh was 49.24 ± 5.84 μM and upper limit of detection was 358.01 μM
outcomes.notes: One mouse (sub-1) of the paper's three, 8 concentrations from 0.000714 to 714 uM. Over 80 readings (ROI tissue or whole frame, 0.55 or 0.50 s frames, two photobleaching fits, two baselines, five rate windows) Km is 0.031 to 0.73 uM and Vmax 8.3 to 49.7 %/s, none within tolerance (49.24 +- 5.84 uM, 281.00 +- 7.14 %/s); R2 0.01 to 0.73. The first reading gives rates of 0.3 to 16.3 %/s with no steady rise in concentration (Spearman rho 0.54, p 0.168), with one-frame steps of 23.1% at 0.000714 uM, 19.8% at 0.714 uM, 41.9% at 7.14 uM and 38.4% at 714 uM, none at 0.00714 and 0.0714 uM. In the six recordings with a step the signal drifts down by 1.5 to 15.5% before it, then jumps within one frame and stays high, so the steps may come in part from adding the solution; the files cannot tell. With one onset (frame 7) for every recording, Km is 0.545 uM and Vmax 11.4 %/s. Upper limit of detection of the first fit 1.92 uM (88% of Vmax) or 0.96 uM (tangent within 5%); the paper's constants give 361.1 and 181.3 uM by the same rules. Measured values are the first reading's Km, Vmax, R2 and reading (a) of the upper limit.
deviations: One of three mice and 8 of the paper's concentrations (to 714 uM, not 7.14 mM) are deposited; means over mice and all points are the same here.

Assumed that ACh was added just before the largest one-frame rise of each recording, as the addition time is not recorded; at 0.00714 and 0.0714 uM there is no clear step, so this onset is noise there.
The ROI is not given; the stained tissue (Otsu mask of the first frame) and the whole frame were run.
Frame interval run at 0.55 s (Results, Ex vivo calibration, "0.55 s, the minimum sampling time") and at 0.50 s, the interval the per-frame timestamps of sub-2 and sub-3 record.

Photobleaching correction by a monoexponential curve, each value divided by the curve (Methods, Animal Preparation and Imaging); the frames it is fit to are open, and both readings of the claims file (frames outside the response, whole trace) were run.
Rate reading (a) fits from the last frame before the response to the peak, so that a rise within one frame is included; reading (b) over the first 2 to 5 frames.

outcomes.statement: The lower limit of detection is 228 nM, where two regression lines through the low-concentration data (0.71 nM to 14.28 uM) cross; the theoretical response there from the Michaelis-Menten equation (1.3 %/s, 0.72% per 0.55 s frame) is 8.18 times the background noise of 0.088 ± 0.039%.
outcomes.source: Results, Ex vivo calibration of the ACh nanosensors, paragraph 2; Figure 4B(ii) legend; Methods, Ex vivo ACh calibration
outcomes.quote: experimental data in the lower con-centration range (i.e., 0.71 nM to 14.28 μM) was grouped into two linear regions with the two regression lines crossing at a value of [ACh] = 228 nM
outcomes.notes: Five deposited concentrations up to 14.28 uM (0.000714 to 7.14 uM). None of 160 crossings (80 rate readings by linear and log concentration) is within 205.2 to 250.8 nM; medians -140 nM (linear) and 3.11 nM (log); the first reading gives 0.977 nM. Baseline noise 1.77 +- 2.34% by SD and 1.17 +- 0.95% by frame-to-frame change, against the paper's 0.088%. The paper's own response at 228 nM (0.712% per 0.55 s) would have a signal-to-noise ratio of 0.40 or 0.61 at this noise; the fit of this mouse gives 0.01 to 0.02. Measured are the first reading's crossing (nM), noise (a) and signal-to-noise (a).
deviations: Reading (c), the split of Figure 4B(ii), was not run, as it needs the figure's lines and the entry reads no figures.
Rests on the rates and onset assumption of fig4b-michaelis-menten, one mouse of three.

outcomes.statement: Normalising the initial rate by the local nanosensor concentration (from AF647 intensity) gives an almost identical Michaelis-Menten curve, EC50 50.35 ± 6.76 uM and Vmax 0.3991 %/(s nM), whose double reciprocal form is Equation 3, 1/V = 126.41/[ACh] + 2.499.
outcomes.source: Results, Ex vivo calibration of the ACh nanosensors, paragraph 2; Equation 3; Figure S6B to D
outcomes.quote: The Vunit sensor–[ACh] relationship was further analyzed by the Michaelis–Menten equation (SI Appendix, Fig. S6B), which showed an almost identical curve to Fig. 4B with an EC50 value of 50.35 ± 6.76 μM.
outcomes.notes: Needs the AF647 intensity of each calibration ROI and the AF647 calibration on nanosensors of known concentration. The sub-1 recordings hold one channel (509 x 255 pixels, half of the camera frame) and no calibration series is deposited. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: The control nanosensor (pHAb and BTX, no AChE) in tissue rises from 18.50 ± 9.74% at pH 7 to 180.43 ± 17.67% at pH 5, with a pKa of 6.10, close to the 6.2 of free pHAb.
outcomes.source: Results, Ex vivo calibration of the ACh nanosensors, paragraph 3; Figure 4C; Figure S7A
outcomes.quote: The signal change from pH 7 to 5 ranged from 18.50 ± 9.74% to 180.43 ± 17.67% with a pKa of 6.10 (Fig. 4C), in accordance with the pKa value of 6.2 represent-ing free pHAb fluorophores
outcomes.notes: Needs the ex vivo recordings of control nanosensors under buffers of pH 3.5 to 9 and the free pHAb curve of Figure S7A. Neither dataset holds pH data or control nanosensor recordings. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: In vivo, lingual nerve stimulation (3 V, 10 Hz, 10 ms, 100 pulses) raises nanosensor fluorescence by 3.7% by 15 s with initial rate 0.294 ± 0.116 %/s, recovering to baseline within 2 min (three mice).
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: Upon the stimulation of the lingual nerve, fluorescence intensity increased 3.7% by 15 s with initial velocity of Vsensor = 0.294 ± 0.116%/s, which slowly recovered to baseline within 2 min (Fig. 5B).
outcomes.notes: Two 3 V, 100-pulse recordings of the ACh nanosensor are deposited, sub-2 and sub-6 after washout; which recordings form the three mice of Figure 5B is not stated. Under 144 readings (frame interval, three bleaching fits, baseline, four ROIs including the tissue less the camera's dark level, recording or their mean) the dF/F 15 s after onset is 17.1 to 40.1%, none within 3.33 to 4.07%; the rate to the peak is 1.54 to 3.33 %/s, and the rates over 2 to 5 frames from the frame where each trace leaves baseline (frames 25 to 29) -0.81 to 4.20 %/s, none within 0.294 +- 0.116 %/s. Rates over 2 to 5 frames from frame 19 fall within it in 54 readings, but they cover baseline frames before the response and are not counted. Cell-sized 40 x 40 pixel blocks give 11.3 to 53.6% (sub-2) and 0.3 to 28.4% (sub-6); one of the 13 sub-6 blocks is within tolerance in both. At 120 s sub-2 is still 9.4 to 16.4% above baseline. Subtracting the dark level raises dF/F slightly (mean of both, tissue, 20.8 to 23.2% without and 21.9 to 24.4% with). Measured values are the mean of the two recordings under the first reading (0.50 s, bleaching fit outside the response, mean baseline, tissue ROI).
deviations: Assumed that the deposited 3 V recordings stand for the three mice of Figure 5B; the deposit does not identify them, and sub-2 is the 3 V recording of the AQuA mouse.

The ROI is a hand-drawn ganglion cell in the paper (Fig. 5B legend) with no coordinates; tissue, whole frame, tissue without saturating pixels, tissue less the camera's dark level and 40 x 40 pixel blocks were run.

Stimulation onset taken as 10.45 s, frame 19 on the paper's 0.55 s clock, from Fig. 6A ("Sti starts 10.45 s") and Fig. 7A ("Stim starts 10.45 s"); the files do not record it. The responses start 4 to 13 frames after it in sub-2, sub-3 and sub-6.
Frame interval run at 0.55 s (Results, Ex vivo calibration, "0.55 s, the minimum sampling time") and at 0.50 s, the interval the per-frame timestamps of sub-2 and sub-3 record.

Photobleaching correction by a monoexponential curve, each value divided by the curve (Methods, Animal Preparation and Imaging); the frames it is fit to are open, and the frames before onset with those from 120 s or from 180 s after it, and the whole trace, were run.

Initial rate over k frames counted from the last frame before the trace leaves baseline (|z| > 5), as the responses start 6 to 10 frames after the assumed stimulation onset; the rates from frame 19 are shown and not counted.
Channel taken as pHAb is the right half in sub-2 (the half that rises), the single channel in sub-6.

outcomes.statement: Control nanosensors (no AChE) show a minimal response to the same 3 V stimulation, so intrinsic pH fluctuation is negligible.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: In contrast, we observed a minimal response when control nanosensors were tested, dem-onstrating that the influence of intrinsic pH fluctuation is negli-gible.
outcomes.notes: Needs in vivo recordings of the control nanosensor at 3 V. Every in vivo recording in SPARC:108 is of the ACh nanosensor (subjects sheet and manifest descriptions); no control recording is deposited.

outcomes.statement: At 10 V stimulation the control nanosensor responds with about 50% of the ACh nanosensor's signal, suggesting a pH change at higher stimulation.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure S8
outcomes.quote: upon stimulation with a higher 10 V voltage, control nanosensors responded to ∼50% of the ACh nanosensor signal intensity (SI Appendix, Fig. S8)
outcomes.notes: Needs paired 10 V recordings of the ACh and control nanosensors (Figure S8). Only one 10 V recording, of the ACh nanosensor (sub-4), is deposited.

outcomes.statement: In one ROI of one animal the initial rate grows with stimulation voltage, 0.1886 %/s at 3 V, 3.24 %/s at 5 V and 11.35 %/s at 10 V.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure 5C
outcomes.quote: with 3 V stimulation increasing 0.1886%/s, 5 V increasing 3.24%/s, and 10 V increasing 11.35%/s, all collected at the same ROI in the ganglia (Fig. 5C)
outcomes.notes: Needs 3, 5 and 10 V recordings in the same ROI of one animal. The deposit has 3 V and 8 V in one ganglion (sub-2, sub-3) and 10 V in another mouse recorded in July 2019 (sub-4); there is no 5 V recording.

outcomes.statement: Through Equation 3, the unit rates at 3, 5 and 10 V (0.0214, 0.0711 and 0.2448 %/(nM s)) give endogenous ACh concentrations of 2.75, 10.49 and 76.51 uM.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 2; Figure 5C; Equation 3
outcomes.quote: we estimated the endogenous ACh concentrations to be 2.75 μM at 3 V, 10.49 μM at 5 V, and 76.51 μM at 10 V
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig5c-voltage-dose and figs6b-unit-calibration, both blocked for missing data; the AF647 calibration is not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Increasing the number of pulses (10, 50, 100 at 3 V) increases the nanosensor response in the same ROI.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure 5D
outcomes.quote: Similarly, increasing the number of pulses also led to a higher ACh nanosensor response (Fig. 5D).
outcomes.notes: Needs recordings with 10, 50 and 100 pulses at 3 V in one ROI. All deposited 3 V recordings are single stimulations, and none is labelled with another pulse number.

outcomes.statement: Three repeated stimulations (10 V, 10 Hz, 10 ms, 10 pulses) in the same ROI give repeatable initial rates of 0.436, 0.417 and 0.431 %/s (0.428 ± 0.010 %/s).
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure 5E
outcomes.quote: showing repeatable rates of 0.436%/s, 0.417%/s, and 0.431%/s in sequence (0.428 ± 0.010%/s, Fig. 5E)
outcomes.notes: Needs one recording with three repeated 10 V, 10-pulse stimulations. The only 10 V recording (sub-4, 509 frames) shows a single response.

outcomes.statement: In vitro, in a dialysis fiber, the nanosensor responds repeatedly to five injections of 100 uM ACh, recovering after each washout.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 1; Figure S7B; Methods, Characterization of ACh nanosensors
outcomes.quote: Reversibility of the sensor was demonstrated by three repeated stimulations ... which was confirmed with in vitro experiments (SI Appendix, Fig. S7B).
outcomes.notes: Needs the confocal recording of nanosensors in a dialysis fiber with five ACh injections. Not in either dataset. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

outcomes.statement: Vesamicol cuts the nanosensor response to 3 V stimulation; in the example the response with the drug is 17% of that after washout, and over four experiments the reduction averages 76.59 ± 11.34%, significant in each by a paired t test (P < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo imaging of ACh release, paragraph 3; Figure 6A to C
outcomes.quote: Four independent inhibitor treatments affirmed that vesamicol can considerably suppress ACh nanosensors' readout by an average of 76.59 ± 11.34% (Fig. 6C)

statistics.test: paired t test, vesamicol treated against untreated

outcomes.notes: One experiment of four is deposited (sub-6, with drug then after washout, one field). Over 48 readings the peak with vesamicol is 11.3 to 29.9% of the washout peak, a reduction of 70.1 to 88.7%, within 76.59 +- 11.34% in 44. Under six readings (two bleaching fits, three ROIs) the AF647 half rises by at most 0.4 to 3.7% after onset, within its pre-stimulus mean plus 3 SD (1.9 to 4.1%), while the pHAb half rises by 46.9 to 54.0%, 14 to 135 times more. The SPARC:108 version 1 manifest holds HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files, eight ex vivo calibration recordings of sub-1, in vivo recordings of sub-2 (3 V), sub-3 (8 V), sub-4 (10 V), the confocal stack of sub-5 and the vesamicol pair of sub-6; SPARC:75 holds six confocal LSM images.

findings.statement: SPARC:108 holds only part of the data the paper reports. Deposited are one of three ex vivo calibration mice (8 concentrations, none above 714 uM), one of four vesamicol experiments, the 3 V and 8 V recordings of the AQuA mouse, one 10 V recording, the nanosensor HPLC, UV-Vis and gel files and one confocal stack. Not deposited are every control nanosensor recording (Fig. 4C, 5B, S8, S10), the pH calibrations (Fig. 4C, S7A), the 5 V, pulse-number and repeated stimulations (Fig. 5C to E), the AF647 concentration calibration (Fig. S6B), the AFM images (Fig. S3), the spectra of pure AChE and BTX (Fig. 2G), the retention, stability, fiber and two-photon images (Fig. 3B-C, S4, S7B, S13) and two of the three 3 V AQuA mice (Fig. S12). Sixteen of the 29 claims are blocked for missing data and one for missing metadata.

The imaging recordings lack what is needed to analyse them. No file says which half of the W-VIEW GEMINI frame is pHAb and which AF647; no file gives a spatial scale (the camera calibration is in pixels); the stimulation onset and the time of ACh addition are not recorded; and the files resaved in ImageJ (sub-1, sub-4, sub-6) keep only the first frame's timestamp, so their frame interval is unknown. The paper gives the onset only as 10.45 s in two figures, and sub-4 does not follow it (its response starts near frame 55 or later).

The primary manifest.xlsx of SPARC:108 describes its files under names that are not in the dataset (40 of 50 differ, for example sub-1/0.000714_uM.tif for sub-1/sub-1_0.000714 uM); seven of the eight calibration files lack the .tif extension; and the sheet describes the sub-1 calibration recordings, made with added ACh, as "ACh release by electrical stimulation".

subjects.xlsx lists sub-2 (3 V) and sub-3 (8 V) as two mice, but their recordings were made 14 minutes apart on one day and show the same field (mean images r = 0.93 with no shift, against 0.06 to 0.47 between other recordings), as the paper's one mouse stimulated at 3 and 8 V (Methods, AQuA Analysis).

The per-frame timestamps of the in vivo recordings that keep them (sub-2, sub-3) give an interval of 0.50 s, while the paper states 0.55 s as its sampling interval and its Figure 7 times are multiples of 0.55 s. Rates in %/s differ by 10% between the two.

Many pixels saturate at 65535 in the sub-6 vesamicol recordings (19.6% of tissue pixels at some frame with the drug, 69.0% after washout) and in the pHAb half of sub-2 and sub-3 (11.5% and 16.4%), which clips the responses the paper's Figure 6 ratio is computed from.

Neither dataset names the PNAS paper. SPARC:108's dataset_description gives the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2020.07.06.189696) as its originating article, and SPARC:75 gives none, so its link to the paper (Figure S5 and the nanosensor staining) rests on its content.

disagreements.reason: Would call it partially reproduced at most. It passes only under reading (ii), timed from each region's onset (30 of 36 variants). Those onsets come 2.75 to 3.3 s after the paper's for the rostral region, and the parent claim matches 0 of 6 times. Timed from the stimulus, reading (i), it fits in 0 of 36 variants and 0 of 157 blocks. Reading (ii) applied to the paper's own Fig. 7B times gives 8.8 s for the rostral region (22.0 - 13.20), outside 9 to 16.5 s. The claims file flags the paper's contradiction only for the caudal region.

The criterion grants partial "when two of three show the order". Only one mouse is deposited, so that threshold cannot be reached. The amplitude part holds (6 of 6 readings), and the order holds in 12 of 18 variants on the median onset and 11 of 18 on the earliest block. These results should be reported without the label "partial", or the claim should be blocked for the two missing mice. The direction of propagation also depends wholly on an orientation checked outside the notebook.

paper_notes.statement: Figure S2C calls itself the same gel as Figure 2E but labels lane 1 as unpurified ACh nanosensor, where Figure 2E has the DNA scaffold. In the deposited gel, lane 1 has a single pHAb band and no AF647 band, as a scaffold without BTX would, so Figure S2C's label looks wrong.

Questions for the authors. (1) Over which frames is the initial rate (Vsensor) taken, from which onset, and against which baseline; and when was ACh added in each calibration recording and the stimulation started in each in vivo recording? Assumed here, onset at the largest one-frame rise (ex vivo) and at 10.45 s (in vivo, from Fig. 6A and 7A), with every rate window the claims file names. (2) Which ROI was used in Figures 5B and 6B, and which deposited recordings are the three mice of Figure 5B? Here the tissue, the whole frame and cell-sized blocks were run, giving 17.1 to 40.1% against 3.7%. (3) Which frame interval applies, the 0.55 s of the paper or the 0.50 s the files record? (4) Which flow rate was used for the HPLC (none is stated, so the retention volumes could not be tested), and how were the peaks of Figure 2D integrated, given that the main peak and the second peak overlap and that the share is 65.8 to 68.2% with a flat baseline and 77.5 to 83.1% with a line under each peak? (5) Which frames was the photobleaching curve fit to? (6) Which AQuA version and parameters were used for Figure 7 and Figures S9 to S12, and where are the four numbered areas of Figure 7A? Block onsets were used in its place here, on the frame as deposited; does rostral lie at the top of the deposited frames, as Fig. 7A shows them? (7) How is the background of the puncta threshold of Figure 3D defined?

entries.name: xia-2021
entries.title: Imaging acetylcholine release with a DNA nanosensor (Xia et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Xia, Yang, Mu, Micovic, Poskanzer, Monaghan and Clark (2021) on SPARC:108, which holds the nanosensor's HPLC, UV-Vis and gel data, ex vivo calibration recordings of one mouse, in vivo recordings at 3, 8 and 10 V, a confocal stack of a stained ganglion and one vesamicol experiment, and on SPARC:75, which holds confocal images of a ganglion stained with BTX or the nanosensor. The control nanosensor, pH, voltage and pulse series, AFM, stability and two-photon data are not deposited, and the AQuA analysis was not run.
